abstract: This first part in a two-part series examines the test facilities available at the University at Buffalo, Buffalo, New York. abstract: The history and the future of backing materials in mica-paper based insulations is examined in this article presented at the 5th BEAMA Conference.

abstract: Recent developments permit the use of dielectric properties measurements to gauge the cure of thermosetting resins under real-time operating conditions.

abstract: This article shows the interpretation of megohmmeter tests in electrical apparatus and circuits to ensure that insulation used in cables, motors, and switchgear is sound.

articleTitle: Advances in Fire Hazard Testing of Electrical Equipment
abstract: Any presentation The past two to three decades have seen vast improvement in fire hazard testing of electrical equipment. International organizations such as IEC and ISO compile the standards. This article examines the latest advances in this exciting field.

articleTitle: Flexible Laminates: Key Insulation for Motors and Generators
abstract: The use of flexible laminates (the bonding together of two or more flexible substrates to form a thin, strong insulation material) as a key insulation source for motors and generators is explained.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Diagnostic Monitoring of Electrical Machines
abstract: RF diagnostic monitoring should make it possible to improve machine maintenance schedules and achieve more time in service.

articleTitle: Field Measurements of Partial Discharges in Potential Transformers
abstract: A recent increase of failures of high voltage potential transformers, due to insulation breakdowns, cause great concern in the utility industry. The need for in situ testing of installed instrument transformers to confirm the loss or remaining quality of the insulation material has led to the adoption of well-established laboratory test methods for applications in electrical substations.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Solvent Versus Solventless Electrical Insulating Varnishes via Systems Testing
abstract: As systems testing becomes more and more engrained in the electrical industry, studies involving single component changes in the design of a system become most important. Cases in which ground and phase insulations have been substituted have had a good deal of work on them. These cases have been done to show the equivalence of substituted products versus standard products which were originally tested. This study involves the substitution of electrical insulating varnishes. The testing instituted the use of abbreviated sets of samples which were tested side by side.

In previous issues of this column, a series of topics concerned with particular phenomena that affect the reliability of electrical insulation were discussed. But the author in this issue, because he has just returned from the CIGRE conference, will take a somewhat different approach and comment on some of the CIGRE activities and papers relevant to insulation reliability. CIGRE is the acronym for Conference Internationale Grande Reseaux Electrique or in English: International Conference on Large Electric Systems, specifically, the electric utility systems of the nations of the world. It is a formal organization with principal representatives appointed by the National Committees of each member nation.

The topic of electrical conduction in electrical insulation was introduced in the previous column of this series. There, the magnitude of conduction was discussed in relation to dielectric heating and attenuation of higher frequency communication signals. In this column the effect of conduction will be discussed in relation to voltage stress distribution and possibly consequent dielectric breakdown initiation by exceeding the breakdown stress of one of the series components.

In the two previous columns in this series, the problem of conduction in insulation was discussed in relation to dielectric heating and electric stress distribution in the insulation system. In this issue, the problem of conducting particles or inclusions in insulation is discussed. Conducting defects are perhaps an obvious deficiency; it is surprising how often this problem is overlooked in selecting or designing insulation.

A brief history is presented of the Westinghouse Electric Corporation. The corporation was formed in 1886 to develop and market alternating current (ac) generation and distribution equipment, has grown and diversified to become a US$10.2 billion business manufacturing and marketing a wide range of products and services.
